category.title: Sliding Window & Pointers
category.description: Two pointers, fixed and variable size sliding window patterns.

algorithms.title: Maximum Sum Subarray of Size K (Fixed Window)
algorithms.summary: Find maximum sum of any contiguous subarray of fixed size K by maintaining rolling window sum in O(1) time per step.
explanation: 1. Compute initial sum of first K elements as initial `window_sum`.
2. Slide window from index K to N-1: add incoming element `arr[i]` and subtract outgoing `arr[i - K]`.
3. Track global maximum `max_sum = max(max_sum, window_sum)`.

wAnswers.whatItSolves: Finds maximal sum across all contiguous windows of fixed length K.
wAnswers.whenToUse: When finding optimal fixed-size contiguous subarray metrics.
wAnswers.whereUsed: Moving averages, audio signal windowing, throughput monitoring.
wAnswers.whyOptimal: O(N) time and O(1) space by updating rolling sum incrementally.

codeTemplates.code:
def maxSumSubarray(arr: list[int], k: int) -> int:
    if len(arr) < k: return 0
    window_sum = sum(arr[:k])
    max_sum = window_sum
    for i in range(k, len(arr)):
        window_sum += arr[i] - arr[i - k]
        max_sum = max(max_sum, window_sum)
    return max_sum

algorithms.title: Average of Window (Maximum Average Subarray I)
algorithms.summary: Find contiguous subarray of length K that has maximum average value.
explanation: 1. Calculate total sum for first K elements.
2. Maintain max sum found so far.
3. Slide window through array: add `nums[i]`, subtract `nums[i-k]`.
4. Return `max_sum / k` as floating point average.

wAnswers.whatItSolves: Locates the window of size K with maximal average score.
wAnswers.whenToUse: When finding peak performance rate over constant time intervals.
wAnswers.whereUsed: CPU load averaging, moving average technical indicators.
wAnswers.whyOptimal: O(N) time single pass avoiding recalculating window sums.

codeTemplates.code:
def findMaxAverage(nums: list[int], k: int) -> float:
    curr_sum = sum(nums[:k])
    max_sum = curr_sum
    for i in range(k, len(nums)):
        curr_sum += nums[i] - nums[i - k]
        max_sum = max(max_sum, curr_sum)
    return max_sum / k

algorithms.title: Maximum/Minimum Window (Sliding Window Maximum)
algorithms.summary: Find maximum element in each sliding window of size K using Monotonic Deque.
explanation: 1. Maintain a double-ended queue (deque) storing indices of potential maximum elements in decreasing order.
2. Remove indices out of current window scope `[i - K + 1]`.
3. Pop smaller elements from back of deque before pushing current element index `i`.
4. Deque front always stores index of maximum element for current window.

exampleTrace.title: Trace on [1,3,-1,-3,5,3,6,7], K=3
traceSteps: i=4 (val 5): pop out of scope 1, pop smaller 2,3 -> deque=[4] -> Max = 5

wAnswers.whatItSolves: Computes rolling maximum/minimum over streaming windows in O(N) linear time.
wAnswers.whenToUse: When finding max/min element in fixed-length dynamic intervals.
wAnswers.whereUsed: Real-time maximum price tracking, rate limit burst monitoring.
wAnswers.whyOptimal: Each index pushed/popped at most once, yielding O(N) time.

algorithms.title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters (Variable Window)
algorithms.summary: Find length of longest substring with all distinct characters using Variable-Size Window and Last-Seen Hash Map.
explanation: 1. Expand `right` pointer index through string.
2. If `s[right]` was seen at index >= `left`, jump `left = last_seen[s[right]] + 1`.
3. Update `last_seen[s[right]] = right` and calculate `max_len = max(max_len, right - left + 1)`.

exampleTrace.title: Trace on "abcabcbb"
traceSteps: right=3 ('a'): Duplicate 'a'! Jump left = 1. Window = "bca", len=3

wAnswers.whatItSolves: Finds maximal length window containing zero duplicate characters.
wAnswers.whenToUse: When finding unique character contiguous sub-segments.
wAnswers.whereUsed: Token parsing, unique string compression algorithms.
wAnswers.whyOptimal: O(N) time single pass with instantaneous pointer updates.

algorithms.title: Smallest Substring (Minimum Window Substring)
algorithms.summary: Find smallest substring in S that contains all characters and frequencies of string T.
explanation: 1. Build character frequency map for pattern string T.
2. Expand `right` pointer to include characters in current window.
3. Once window covers all required frequencies (`formed == required`), shrink `left` pointer to minimize window length.
4. Record global minimum substring bounds.

exampleTrace.title: Trace S="ADOBECODEBANC", T="ABC"
traceSteps: Expand right to 5 ("ADOBEC"): All 'A', 'B', 'C' matched! Window len=6
Expand right to index 12 ("BANC"): All matched! Window len=4

wAnswers.whatItSolves: Finds smallest substring containing specified multiset of target characters.
wAnswers.whenToUse: When finding minimal enclosing range meeting frequency requirements.
wAnswers.whereUsed: DNA motif matching, query term search snippet extraction.
wAnswers.whyOptimal: O(N+M) expansion/contraction avoiding redundant full-string scans.

codeTemplates.code:
from collections import Counter

def minWindow(s: str, t: str) -> str:
    if not s or not t: return ""
    target_map = Counter(t)
    required = len(target_map)
    left = 0
    formed = 0
    window_counts = {}
    min_len = float('inf')
    ans_bounds = (0, 0)
    for right, ch in enumerate(s):
        window_counts[ch] = window_counts.get(ch, 0) + 1
        if ch in target_map and window_counts[ch] == target_map[ch]:
            formed += 1
        while left <= right and formed == required:
            if right - left + 1 < min_len:
                min_len = right - left + 1
                ans_bounds = (left, right)
            l_ch = s[left]
            window_counts[l_ch] -= 1
            if l_ch in target_map and window_counts[l_ch] < target_map[l_ch]:
                formed -= 1
            left += 1
    return "" if min_len == float('inf') else s[ans_bounds[0]:ans_bounds[1]+1]

algorithms.title: Longest Substring with At Most K Distinct Characters
algorithms.summary: Find maximum length subarray/substring containing at most K distinct elements.
explanation: 1. Expand `right` pointer and record character frequencies in a map.
2. If `map.size() > K`, shrink window from `left` until distinct count <= K.
3. Update max length: `max_len = max(max_len, right - left + 1)`.

exampleTrace.title: Trace S="eceba", K=2
traceSteps: right=3 ('b'): map has 3 keys! Shrink left=0 -> map={'c':1, 'b':1}, len=2

wAnswers.whatItSolves: Finds maximal contiguous window containing up to K unique symbols.
wAnswers.whenToUse: When distinct key count bounds the active working set.
wAnswers.whereUsed: LRU cache hot-key window tracking, variable symbol compression.

algorithms.title: Subarrays with Exactly K Distinct Elements
algorithms.summary: Count contiguous subarrays containing exactly K distinct elements using formula: `Exactly(K) = AtMost(K) - AtMost(K - 1)`.
explanation: 1. Direct sliding window directly for 'Exactly K' is difficult because shrinking left can invalidate validity.
2. Key Reducer Pattern: `Count(Exactly K) = Count(At Most K) - Count(At Most K - 1)`.
3. Implement helper `atMostK(nums, k)` using sliding window.
4. Return `atMostK(nums, k) - atMostK(nums, k - 1)`.

exampleTrace.title: Trace nums=[1,2,1,2,3], K=2
traceSteps: atMostK(nums, 2): counts total subarrays with <= 2 distinct = 12
atMostK(nums, 1): counts total subarrays with <= 1 distinct = 5
Result: 12 - 5 = 7 subarrays with exactly 2 distinct numbers.

wAnswers.whatItSolves: Counts exact frequency constrained subarrays via AtMost dual subtraction.
wAnswers.whenToUse: When finding exact count of subarrays meeting distinct bounds.
wAnswers.whereUsed: Data stream partitioning, user session segmentation.
wAnswers.whyOptimal: O(N) time linear double-pass sliding window.

algorithms.title: Find All Anagrams in a String (Frequency Window)
algorithms.summary: Find all start indices of p's anagrams in s using fixed-size frequency array window.
explanation: 1. Maintain target frequency array `p_count` of size 26 for string `P`.
2. Maintain running window frequency array `s_count` of size 26 for string `S`.
3. Slide window of size `len(P)` across `S`. At each step, compare `s_count == p_count`.
4. If matched, append window start index to result array.

wAnswers.whatItSolves: Locates all occurrences of string permutations in target text.
wAnswers.whenToUse: When finding anagrams or permutations within long text streams.
wAnswers.whereUsed: Bioinformatics DNA sequence motif matching, plagiarism checking.
wAnswers.whyOptimal: O(N) time with O(26) = O(1) space.

algorithms.title: Longest Repeating Character Replacement
algorithms.summary: Find length of longest substring containing same letter after replacing at most K characters.
explanation: 1. Window Invariant: `window_length - max_char_frequency <= K`.
2. Maintain character frequency map and track max frequency character `max_freq` in current window.
3. Expand `right` pointer. If `(right - left + 1) - max_freq > K`, shrink window by advancing `left++`.
4. Calculate `max_len = max(max_len, right - left + 1)`.

wAnswers.whatItSolves: Finds maximal uniform character segment achievable with at most K edits.
wAnswers.whenToUse: When optimizing string homogenization under replacement budget.

algorithms.title: Permutation in String (Check Inclusion)
algorithms.summary: Check if string s2 contains any permutation of string s1 as a substring.
explanation: 1. Build target character count array for string s1.
2. Slide a window of size `len(s1)` across string s2.
3. Compare running frequency count with target frequency count.
4. Return True if any window matches target frequency, else False.

wAnswers.whatItSolves: Determines if any anagram of pattern exists within host string.
wAnswers.whereUsed: Password strength pattern checking, virus signature scanning.
wAnswers.whyOptimal: O(N) sliding window with O(1) frequency array equality checks.

codeTemplates.code:
def checkInclusion(s1: str, s2: str) -> bool:
    if len(s1) > len(s2): return False
    c1, c2 = [0] * 26, [0] * 26
    for i in range(len(s1)):
        c1[ord(s1[i]) - ord('a')] += 1
        c2[ord(s2[i]) - ord('a')] += 1
    if c1 == c2: return True
    for i in range(len(s1), len(s2)):
        c2[ord(s2[i]) - ord('a')] += 1
        c2[ord(s2[i - len(s1)]) - ord('a')] -= 1
        if c1 == c2: return True
    return False
